subject: Food Science
title: Spice Heat and Capsaicin
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Spice Heat and Capsaicin.

hook.text: Capsaicin doesn't create a taste—it triggers pain receptors. The 'heat' from chili peppers is literally your body signaling.

buildup.text: Capsaicin binds to TRPV1 receptors, the same receptors that detect scalding heat above 43°C.

discovery.text: Birds lack TRPV1 sensitivity to capsaicin—they eat peppers without pain. Plants evolved capsaicin to deter mammals but attract.

twist.text: Capsaicin is fat-soluble, not water-soluble. Drinking water doesn't help—it spreads the capsaicin.

climax.text: Repeated chili exposure desensitizes TRPV1 receptors. Spice tolerance is real and trainable.

punchline.text: Chili 'heat' is pain, not flavor. Water won't help—drink milk. And birds feel nothing.

quiz.question: Why does water not relieve the burn from capsaicin?
options: Capsaicin is fat-soluble—water can't dissolve it and just spreads it around
